chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The womb (kinship) is suspended by the Throne on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O Allah! Maintain the one who maintains me, and cut off the one who cuts me off'.
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the status of kinship on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi personifies kinship (al-Rahim) as a supplicant hanging from the Divine Throne, emphasizing the cosmic weight of maintaining family ties in Shia tradition. It underscores the spiritual consequence of severing relationships, linking social ethics directly to divine judgment and mercy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The womb (kinship of the Progeny<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>) would attach itself to the Throne on the Day of Judgement, saying, ‘O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Maintain with the one who maintained me, and Cut off from the one who cut me off’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Kindred relation will hold to the Throne (of the Lord) on the Day of Judgment and say, “O Lord, establish good relations with those who establish me and cut off good relations with those who cut me off.’”
